title: [CQ-R14d3] Check session over the SSH route
description:
Sixth slice of task-fd196d137c44497188d2639f149e259b (DESIGN comment-350cb4d0, governor ruling comment-d954b3df). It depends on R14d1 (task-b8734a78) for openGuestStream, and it shares local-runner.test.mjs with R14d1. It touches neither file of R14d2 (task-5e2dcd2c), so the two can run in parallel.

**Objective.** runCheckSession runs the supervisor's check mode over OpenSSH. Certify's watched check sessions must keep the provider fields the route needs. certify's framing session streams about 2 MiB of job stdout, which is the size Windows exec stalls at.

**Deliverable.**
- **The spawn.** In scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs, runCheckSession's child comes from `openGuestStream({name, mode: 'check', provider})`, awaited before the check-frame write.
  - A transport refusal resolves 'infra-failure', with nothing spawned.
  - ssh's own exit 255 resolves 'infra-failure'. It is never treated as 79, 80, 81 or 82, and never as any other supervisor code (ruling condition 5).
  - checkArgv is no longer imported. The export stays until the integration row removes it.
- **Certify pass-through.** watchedSession in scripts/local-runner/certify-bridge.mjs passes `{...context.provider, executable, spawn: watched}` to runCheckSession. Today it rebuilds the provider as `{executable, spawn}`, which would drop `run` (the info read), `ssh` and `keyDir`.
- **Fake-carrier rows** in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs:
  1. a check frame cut short reaches the real supervisor, which refuses, and the result is 'infra-failure';
  2. dead stdin, with no hello, gives 'timeout' when the budget fires;
  3. a stdout stall after hello gives 'timeout';
  4. ssh exit 255 before hello, and again after hello, gives 'infra-failure', with exitCode null;
  5. certify's watchedSession forwards provider.run, ssh and keyDir to the route.
- **Certify assertions.** local-runner.test.mjs certify assertions that expect checkArgv now expect the SSH route.

**Not in scope:** the bridge session (R14d2), transfers (R14d1), removing checkArgv (integration row), guest-supervisor.py and certify's probes and criteria.

**Verification**, in a snapshot and never in place:
`S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD scripts packages/moe-daemon/src packages/moe-daemon/package.json packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json .github | tar -x -C "$S" && cp --parents scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs scripts/local-runner/certify-bridge.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs "$S" && cd "$S" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs`
definitionOfDone: runCheckSession spawns only through openGuestStream with mode 'check'. A row asserts the pinned ssh executable and sshStreamArgv, and that `multipass exec` is never used.
Each of the three measured failure modes has a fake-carrier row ending in 'infra-failure' or 'timeout', as the description lists, and never 'passed' or 'code-failure'.

ssh exit 255 before and after hello each resolve to 'infra-failure' with exitCode null (two rows). A transport refusal resolves to 'infra-failure' with no spawn. Exits 79, 80, 81 and 82 keep their existing outcomes.
certify's watchedSession forwards provider.run, ssh and keyDir to runCheckSession (a row). Every existing C, CJ, CC, CB and certify row stays green, with only its expected executable or argv updated.
The description's verification command exits 0 in the snapshot, under env -i with Node 24.21.0.

No seat runs Multipass. guest-supervisor.py (its sha256 3a19f3bf… is R13's commit-under-test pin), the R02 image pin and every readiness evaluator stay untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Gate 0 first (task rail). Confirm the governor's Gate 0 PASS comment on task-fd196d137c44497188d2639f149e259b covers Windows (a)-(c) and Linux (a)-(d). Without it, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds [] and the reason 'waiting on the governor Gate 0 PASS for the SSH transport', and edit nothing.

Then, in scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs:
(1) Imports. Drop checkArgv from the guest-bridge import (the export stays until fd196d13 removes it). Import openGuestStream from './guest-stream.mjs' and isOwnedInstanceName from './lifecycle.mjs'.
(2) Input checks. The existing condition gains `isOwnedInstanceName(name)`, so a bad name stays CHECK_SESSION_INPUT_INVALID before any spawn, as checkArgv made it. Keep the executable and spawn checks: executable now drives openGuestStream's info read. options becomes { name, provider, frame: checkFrame(check), budgetMs, timeoutMs, signal }.
(3) After the existing pre-spawn abort check: `let child; try { child = await openGuestStream({ name: options.name, mode: 'check', provider: options.provider }); } catch { child = null; }`, then the existing shape check returning result('infra-failure'). A transport refusal therefore spawns nothing.
(4) watch().
  - Right after registering the abort listener, add `if (options.signal?.aborted) s.onAbort();`. An abort during the info read then still kills through stop(s, true), with every listener attached.
  - Write the check frame only when `!s.closing`.
  - The budget still starts at spawn, so the info read never consumes it.
  Error handling:
  - ssh's own exit 255 already ends in outcomeOf as 'infra-failure', and exitCode is null because infra-failure is not OBSERVED.
  - Comment that 79, 80, 81 and 82 can only be the supervisor's own exit relayed by ssh, which uses 255 for its own failures, and that no supervisor code is ever derived from 255 (ruling condition 5).
(5) Update the header and the JSDoc provider line ({executable, run, spawn, ssh, keyDir}) to name the OpenSSH route instead of `multipass exec`.
implementationPlan.note: Gate 0 confirmed: Windows PASS comment-2566639b (a-c) and Linux PASS comment-888759e9 (a-d) on fd196d13; the governor recorded both as satisfying the rail in comment-a88ca3de. check-session.mjs: checkArgv import dropped; openGuestStream + isOwnedInstanceName imported; name validated in the input check; provider frozen-copied ({...provider, executable, spawn}); the only spawn is await openGuestStream({mode:'check'}), and a refusal is 'infra-failure'. watch(): an abort during the info read now tears down; the frame and its deadline are written only while not closing; there is a 255 comment. Header and JSDoc updated. node --check passes. Pre-existing dirty paths of other sessions are untouched.

  - Add a minimal valid INFO detail: { state: 'Running', image_hash: 'a'.repeat(64), image_release: '24.04 LTS', cpu_count: '2', memory: {}, disks: { sda1: {} }, mounts: {}, ipv4: ['10.0.0.2'] }.

  - Add `checkCall = (name = NAME) => [CHECK_SSH, sshStreamArgv({ ...transportFiles(name, CHECK_KEYS), name, address: '10.0.0.2', mode: 'check' }), PIPES]`.

(2) scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (certify and CQ-R11 sections)

So each expectation uses its own harness provider, or R14d1's streamCall where that provider is the STREAM one.
  - Replace every checkArgv(...) session expectation with streamFor or streamCall('check', name). That covers the CB framing, eof and network rows, the containment session.args[1] row (nameAt(8)), the cancel row that pinned windowsPlatform.executable (nameAt(2); the executable becomes that harness provider's ssh), and CJ6's proc.argv.
  - The certify-cancel stub that calls input.provider.spawn('multipass', checkArgv(...)) calls it with streamFor(input.provider, 'check', input.name) instead.
  - CJ6's check-harness provider gains run (fakeGuest's), ssh and keyDir if it lacks them.
  - Each check session adds one info read before its spawn to any asserted provider-call sequence.
  - Drop checkArgv from the CQ-R11 import once unused.

implementationPlan.description:

- CS1. Route.
  - proc.calls deepEqual [checkCall()].
  - The provider's run saw exactly one info call before the spawn, and no argv anywhere contains 'exec'.
- CS2. Transport refusals are 'infra-failure' with proc.calls []:

  - info has ipv4 [];
  - keyDir is 'keys' (relative).
- CS3. Linux truncation against the REAL supervisor's check mode. Reuse the existing real-supervisor spawn behind a stdin-cutting carrier that forwards only the first half of the check frame and then ends the child's stdin.
  - The python child exits nonzero, as recorded.
  - The outcome is 'infra-failure' with exitCode null.
  Gate it exactly like the existing real-supervisor rows.
- CS4. Windows dead stdin. The write callback never fires and no hello comes. budgetMs 100 and timeoutMs 1000, so the budget fires first.
  - The outcome is 'timeout'.
  - kills include 'SIGKILL'.
- CS5. Windows stdout stall. The carrier sends hello and the first half of an output frame, then silence. With budgetMs 100, the outcome is 'timeout'.
- CS6. ssh exit 255.
  - Before hello: 'infra-failure', exitCode null.
  - After hello and one observation: 'infra-failure', exitCode null, never the observed job code.
  - Contrast row over the same carrier: the supervisor's own 79 (no frame), 80 (after the observation), 81 (no frame) and 82 (no frame) keep 'skipped', 'inconclusive', 'infra-failure' and 'code-failure' (exitCode 82, CANDIDATE_REFUSAL).
- CS7. Abort during the info read. run's info waits on a promise; the test aborts and then releases it.
  - The outcome is 'infra-failure'.
  - The check frame was never written: proc.written is empty, and kills include 'SIGKILL'.
- CS8. certify watchedSession pass-through. Import watchedSession from certify-bridge.mjs and call it with context.provider = { executable: E, run: a recording infoRun, ssh: CHECK_SSH, keyDir: CHECK_KEYS, spawn: a recorder }.
  - The recorder got exactly checkCall()'s triple.
  - run saw the info call with executable E.

Assert exact values, never truthiness. Kill only processes the test spawned.

Rejected alternatives:
- Interpreting a 255 after an observation as the job's code. Ruling condition 5 says never.
- Moving the budget start before the info read. The budget is documented as the host's wall clock from spawn, and the info read is already bounded by QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS.

completionSummary:
CQ-R14d3: check sessions run the supervisor's check mode over the pinned OpenSSH stream, never `multipass exec`.

**Runtime**
- check-session.mjs:
  - isOwnedInstanceName joined the input check, so CHECK_SESSION_INPUT_INVALID still comes before any call.
  - The provider is frozen and copied at entry.
  - The only spawn is `await openGuestStream({name, mode:'check', provider})`; a transport refusal or spawn throw is 'infra-failure' with nothing spawned.
  - watch(): an abort that landed during the info read takes stop(s,true), and the frame is written only while not closing.
  - The budget still starts at spawn. ssh 255 is always 'infra-failure' with exitCode null. 79-82 are unchanged.
  - The checkArgv import is dropped; the export and C1 stay for fd196d13.
- certify-bridge.mjs: watchedSession passes `{...context.provider, executable, spawn: watched}`, so run, ssh and keyDir reach the route. The header now names sshStreamArgv instead of snapshotArgv and checkArgv.

**Tests**
- local-runner-check.test.mjs:
  - CHECK_ROUTE and checkCall wiring for hostCheck, C3, C4, C7 and C9.
  - C5 and C8b wait one setImmediate before scripting, because the spawn now follows the async info read.
  - New rows CS1-CS8:
    - CS1: pinned and injected ssh, exact argv, no exec.
    - CS2: 4 refusals, 0 spawns.
    - CS3: real supervisor behind a frame-cutting carrier; python exits 74; infra-failure.
    - CS4: dead stdin gives timeout plus SIGKILL.
    - CS5: stdout stall gives timeout.
    - CS6: 255 before and after hello gives infra-failure with exitCode null; 79-82 contrast.
    - CS7: abort during info; zero writes, SIGKILL.
    - CS8: watchedSession pass-through.
- local-runner.test.mjs:
  - streamFor helper.
  - CB2, CB4, GN1, CC4, LC1, LC2 and CJ6 expect the SSH route; CB2's ids gain one 'info'.
  - containmentRig's session provider aliases its never-launched VM's info read to GUEST (infoAs). This is wiring only, and the change exec keeps its own name.

**Evidence**
- Fresh snap
